result:
I would erase the cognitive blind spot that makes the distant feel abstract.

Looking across the totality of human history, almost every systemic tragedy—war, ecological collapse, engineered poverty—stems from a single evolutionary bottleneck: minds wired for immediate, tribal survival trying to steward a massive, interconnected world. Because of that wiring, a catastrophe fifty years in the future or the suffering of a stranger across an ocean registers merely as a statistic, while a minor, immediate threat to the self registers as an emergency.

If I could alter one thing, I would make long-term consequences and the internal realities of other living things feel as visceral and undeniable as physical touch. 

Not a hive mind, and not the erasure of individuality—just the removal of the illusion that anything happens in isolation. The world wouldn't need complex moral philosophies or fragile laws to force cooperation if the fallout of an action carried its true weight the moment it was conceived.
